newsitem.title: USA: FASB to exempt some companies from disclosure rule.
newsitem.headline: FASB to exempt some companies from disclosure rule.

text.p: The Financial Accounting Standards Board said on Thursday it voted to exempt more companies and not-for-profit organizations from its Statement 107 requirement on disclosures about financial instruments.
Statement 107 requires companies to disclose in a footnote the fair value of all financial instruments which they held.

Non-public companies with less than $100 million in assets and that have not held or issued derivatives, apart from loan commitments, during the reporting period would not be required to apply the provisions of Statement 107, the FASB said.
The proposal would become effective when a final Statement is issued, which is expected to be in December, it said.
